title: Six questions
to ask before
you buy any
AI tool
slides.subtitle: Not what it can do. What it actually replaces, what it costs once you use it, and what happens when it gets something wrong.

slides.label: What job does this replace?
slides.detail: A tool that does everything fixes nothing. If you cannot name the one task it takes off somebody's plate, it becomes another tab nobody opens by week three.
slides.start: Finish the sentence: before, we did this by hand, now this tool does it.

slides.label: Where does our data actually go?
slides.detail: Half of UK founders admit they have put sensitive business data into a public AI tool without checking where it goes. Most never read the setting that decides whether their inputs train someone else's model.
slides.start: Find that tool's own privacy page and check whether your inputs are used for training by default.

slides.label: What does it cost once we actually use it?
slides.detail: The demo price and the real price are rarely the same number. Usage-based tools look cheap at ten requests a day and look very different at the volume a working team actually generates.
slides.start: Run the free trial hard for a week, then project the bill at your real volume, not the demo volume.

slides.label: Can someone else here run it without you?
slides.detail: Only a quarter of UK businesses already using AI have any process in place for it. A tool only you understand is not a system, it is a habit that leaves the building when you do.
slides.start: Hand it to the newest person on the team for a day and watch exactly where they get stuck.

slides.label: What happens when it gets it wrong?
slides.detail: Every AI tool is wrong sometimes. The question that actually matters is who catches it, a person or your customer, and how much it costs when it is the customer.
slides.start: Ask the vendor for one real example of a wrong output and what their product does next.

slides.label: Would we still want this in six months?
slides.detail: Companies abandoning most of their AI tools jumped from 17% to 42% in a single year. Most of that was never a bad tool, it was a tool nobody planned to keep checking on.
slides.start: Put a date in the calendar right now to actually review whether it is still earning its place.

title: Ask all six.
Buy none until you can.
slides.body: The businesses getting real value from AI are not the ones that moved fastest. They are the ones that could answer all six of these about every tool they kept.
slides.cta: Which of these six would you actually struggle to answer about a tool you're using right now?
